Title: Anwar welcomes Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing at Perdana Putra
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 8 — Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing, who is on a two-day visit to Malaysia beginning yesterday, was accorded an official welcome at the Perdana Putra Complex here today.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim welcomed Min Aung Hlaing at about 9am, followed by the playing of the national anthems of both countries.
Min Aung Hlaing then inspected a guard-of-honour mounted by three officers and 103 personnel from the First Battalion, Royal Ranger Regiment, led by Major Muhammad Nur Addeen Mustaza.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim (right) shakes hands with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing following an official welcoming ceremony during the latter’s two-day official visit to Malaysia, at the Perdana Putra Complex in Putrajaya on October 8, 2026. — Bernama pic
The ceremony was also attended by Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Cabinet members, foreign diplomats and senior government officials.
Following the ceremony, Min Aung Hlaing signed the guest book and then proceeded to a private meeting with Anwar, followed by a bilateral meeting involving senior ministers and officials from both countries.
Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing inspects a guard of honour comprising three officers and 103 personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Ranger Regiment, led by Major Muhammad Nur Addeen Mustaza, at the Perdana Putra Complex in Putrajaya on October 8, 2026. — Bernama pic
The two leaders are expected to discuss several key issues, including efforts to repatriate Myanmar nationals of all ethnic groups who are in Malaysia illegally, on a voluntary, dignified and safe basis.
They are also expected to review ongoing efforts being implemented through Asean mechanisms. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia prepares for extreme heat as El Nino looms from end-2026 to April, says Mat Sabu
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 8 — The government is making early preparations for potentially extreme heat, with temperatures forecast to reach 40 degrees Celsius from the end of this year until April next year.
Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said his ministry is also seeking input from experts in artificial intelligence (AI), science and technology to identify the best ways to deal with the expected weather changes.
“We are in the midst of looking for solutions, including from experts in AI technology, science and other fields, on how to deal with temperatures reaching 40 degrees Celsius from the end of this year until April next year, as forecast,” he said at the ‘Dinner with Parti Amanah Negara President’ here yesterday.
He said early preparations were important to ensure that the government and the people would not panic in the event of prolonged hot and dry weather.
Mohamad said one issue that needed attention was the possibility of water shortages, which could affect the agriculture sector, including crop cultivation and livestock activities.
He said early information and weather forecasts were also being taken into account to enable appropriate measures to be planned in advance.
Meanwhile, Mohamad hopes Budget 2027, to be tabled on Friday (October 9), would give attention to the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security in view of the challenges expected to arise from the El Nino phenomenon.
“I think there may be some additional allocation for the Ministry of Agriculture because one of the challenges we will have to face is El Nino next year,” he added.
He said the water supply issue also needed to be addressed early to ensure that the country’s agriculture sector and food security would not be affected in the event of a prolonged period of hot weather. — Bernama

Title: CGT Asia confirms Philippine passenger boarded Subang-Laos flight without carry-on baggage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — CGT Asia Limited has confirmed that only one Philippine national was on board its aircraft when it departed Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport (WMSA), Subang, for Luang Prabang International Airport, Laos, on October 1, and that the passenger boarded without any carry-on luggage.
CGT Asia chief executive officer Captain Darren Chan Chee Seng said the Learjet 55B, registered as N73GP, departed Subang at about 11.30am local time and arrived at Luang Prabang International Airport (VLLB) at about 1.30pm.
He said the passenger was the sole passenger on the WMSA-VLLB sector.
“At the time of departure from WMSA, the passenger boarded the aircraft without presenting any carry-on baggage,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Chan said the operating crew had been informed that the passenger intended to collect luggage containing vape products for the onward flight and that the passenger would personally handle the customs clearance process.
“However, the crew had not been informed that the luggage would consist of approximately 23 pieces, and this quantity was substantially greater than anticipated,” he said.
Upon arrival at VLLB, approximately 23 pieces of luggage were presented for the intended onward flight to Ninoy Aquino International Airport, Manila, Philippines, before the aircraft was scheduled to ferry back to Subang.
Chan said the operating crew was not involved in the customs clearance process but raised operational and safety concerns after becoming aware of the proposed baggage.
These included the unusually large quantity of baggage, the aircraft’s baggage capacity, weight-and-balance considerations applicable to the Learjet 55B, and the possible presence of lithium batteries or other items potentially subject to dangerous goods requirements.
“The luggage was not accepted for carriage and was not loaded onto aircraft N73GP at Luang Prabang International Airport. — Bernama

Title: Orange economy has potential to power growth of Malaysia’s creative sector, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The creative economy sector, which contributes about 6.8 per cent to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP), holds immense potential to become a new driver of the nation’s economic growth, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He noted that advancements in digital technology now allow local creative content such as podcasts, music, animation, video games, and social media content to be exported to global markets, transcending geographical boundaries.
“When we produce a podcast, the audience isn’t limited to those inside the studio. Someone in California can watch it, someone in New Delhi can watch it, and even someone in Vladivostok can watch it,” he said while appearing as a guest on Jangan Kecam podcast hosted by Nazz Abdullah.
Fahmi said this demonstrates significant scope for exporting local content and intellectual property (IP) worldwide, thereby opening up broader revenue opportunities for creative industry players.
He added that this potential has prompted the government to establish the Orange Economy Council to guide and help strengthen the creative industry ecosystem, encompassing sectors such as film, music, video games, e-sports, and animation.
Regarding whether content creators fall under the “orange economy” category, he noted that while they are part of the creative economy, their business models vary and must be understood before specific forms of assistance can be determined.
“Content creation is not a job category with a uniform business model, some generate income through affiliate marketing, product sales, streaming, view counts, advertising, sponsorships, and brand collaborations.
According to him, digital platforms such as TikTok, TikTok Shop, Shopee, Facebook Marketplace, and Lazada also contribute to the growth of the digital economy by providing support and training related to sales, live streaming, and income generation.
Fahmi said issues requiring the government’s attention include copyright and the use of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly when the technology is used to produce content based on the works or identities of intellectual property owners.
“Many content creators are currently asking about AI how to use it, whether they can use tools like Suno or others to create AI-generated music.
“For instance, if we want to use a song by Faizal Tahir, feed it into an AI to create a new track, and then include that AI-generated music in our content is that permissible? In this regard, the government needs to step in and intervene to ensure that the rights of Faizal Tahir and other intellectual property owners are protected and safeguarded,” he said.
Regarding funding for content creators, Fahmi noted that there is currently no specific fund for this group, as the ministry’s support remains largely focused on sectors like film and music, in line with existing policies such as the National Film Policy and the National Broadcasting Policy.
However, he added that the Ministry of Communications, together with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), provides support to eligible mainstream and online media outlets, including through the Media Innovation Fund.
“The amount we allocated last year remains applicable this year which is RM30 million,” he said, explaining that media companies wishing to apply must meet certain criteria, including being registered with the Department of Information as electronic media entities.
Meanwhile, Fahmi urged creative industry players including eligible content creators to take advantage of the tax relief facilities provided by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB), including those for the purchase of business-related equipment.
“To date, no Malaysian content creators’ association has held an official meeting with me to raise specific industry issues; however, the government is open to understanding their needs and challenges,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MOF finalising proposed law to strengthen governance of govt-owned companies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is finalising a proposal to enact the Statutory Bodies and Controlled Entities (Financial Governance) Act to strengthen the governance of government-owned companies.
The ministry said the proposal is expected to impose stricter procedures for the establishment of new companies, strengthen mechanisms for approving investments and loans, and increase the accountability of boards of directors and management.
“The Act aims to ensure that corporate decisions are made prudently, transparently and responsibly,” it said.
MOF said this in a written reply to a question from Azli Yusof (PH-Shah Alam) on measures taken to improve governance following audit reports on leakages of public funds.
In addition to legislative reforms, the ministry said the government is also strengthening compliance with regulations regarding bonus payments and procurement by Federal Statutory Bodies to ensure these matters take into account performance, financial capacity, and the government’s interests.
“The government will also clarify and streamline the jurisdictions for relevant agencies to reduce overlapping functions, close oversight gaps and ensure that monitoring and follow-ups are carried out in a more structured, consistent and effective manner,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Haze persists as 38 areas record unhealthy API, Segamat highest at 187
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Haze continued to blanket much of Peninsular Malaysia this morning, with 38 of the country’s 68 air quality monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 9am, led by Segamat in Johor at 187.
Department of Environment (DOE) data showed Nilai in Negeri Sembilan was next at 183, followed by Seremban at 182, Pasir Gudang at 180 and Kluang at 179.
Johor remained among the worst-hit states, with all eight monitored locations in the unhealthy range, including Larkin (178), Tangkak (172), Pengerang (165), Kota Tinggi (164) and Batu Pahat (161).
In the Klang Valley, unhealthy readings were recorded at Johan Setia (178), Shah Alam (170), Banting (167), Klang (166), Petaling Jaya (165) and Kuala Selangor (155), while Putrajaya stood at 173 and Kuala Lumpur’s Cheras and Batu Muda stations at 172 and 168 respectively.
Meanwhile, Port Dickson recorded an API reading of 168, while all three monitoring stations in Melaka — Bukit Rambai (172), Bandaraya Melaka (171) and Alor Gajah (167) — registered unhealthy air quality.
Unhealthy readings were also recorded at five stations in Perak, four in Pahang, three in Penang, two in Terengganu and one in Kedah, while no station nationwide was in the very unhealthy or hazardous range at 9am.
In contrast, all 21 monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded moderate air quality as of 8am, with Serian at 96, Kuching at 93 and Samarahan at 92.
All schools in Johor are closed today and tomorrow following a decree by the Regent of Johor Tunku Mahkota Ismail after haze and air quality deteriorated across the state.
The Education Ministry has also instructed schools to immediately suspend outdoor activities when API readings exceed 100, while schools in areas where the reading exceeds 200 are to be closed.
MetMalaysia has forecast haze in several affected areas today, including Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Batu Pahat, although the department expects the inter-monsoon period beginning tomorrow to bring weaker winds, thunderstorms and heavy rain that could help ease the cross-border haze.
Under the DOE’s API classification, readings of zero to 50 are considered good, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and above 300 hazardous.

Title: Medical officers’ absence in Sabah, Sarawak and AUKU replacement Bill top Dewan Rakyat agenda today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The failure of medical officers to report for duty in Sabah and Sarawak, as well as the status of a new Bill to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU), are among the main issues to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on the Parliament’s official website, during the Question Time, Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai) will ask the Health Minister to state the actual number of medical officers who failed to report for duty after the deadline yesterday, as well as the reasons and measures to address the issue.
Also scheduled to be raised during the session is a question from Sivakumar Varatharaju Naidu (PH-Batu Gajah) to the Higher Education Minister on the latest developments regarding the drafting of a new bill to replace AUKU 1971, as well as the Government’s commitment to table it in Parliament in December.
Awang Hashim (PN-Pendang) will ask the Finance Minister on the demarcation of jurisdiction between the Securities Commission Malaysia and other regulatory agencies to prevent overlapping functions and enforcement.
Tan Hong Pin (PH-Bakri) will also ask the Digital Minister to provide an update on the ministry’s achievements in strengthening digital literacy and artificial intelligence (AI) skills, as well as its strategic action plan to develop highly skilled digital talent.
Following the question-and-answer session, the Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to continue with the second reading of the Food (Amendment) Bill 2026 by the Health Minister, and the Courts of Judicature (Amendment) Bill 2026 by the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department.
The Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament is being held for 37 days until December 8. — Bernama

Title: Cooking oil subsidies total RM3.886b, palm oil levies RM3.278b in 2024-2025, says MOF
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The government spent RM3.886 billion on cooking oil subsidies from 2024 to 2025, compared with RM3.278 billion collected in windfall profit levies from the palm oil industry during the same period, according to the Ministry of Finance (MoF).
The MoF stated that the collection of windfall profit levies is revenue for the Federal Government and is deposited into the Federal Consolidated Fund, in accordance with Article 97(1) of the Federal Constitution.
“The proceeds from this levy are then reallocated through the annual budget to fund programmes that benefit the people, including the provision of cooking oil subsidies under the Cooking Oil Price Stabilisation Scheme each year,” the ministry said.
The MoF said this in a written response to a question from Bakri Jamaluddin (PN-Tangga Batu) regarding the collection of palm oil industry levies and their usage.
The MoF added that the government continues to subsidise cooking oil to protect the people from rising crude palm oil prices in the market. — Bernama

Title: Govt reviewing formal e-Jamin agreement with Dapat Vista before Cabinet submission, says Kulasegaran
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The government is reviewing a formal agreement with Dapat Vista Sdn Bhd, the company that operates the e-Jamin system for online payment of court bail, before submitting it to the Cabinet soon.
Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said relevant departments were fine-tuning the matter to ensure the agreement includes clear terms on services, accountability and transparency.
“We need to expedite the agreement so that the terms can be made known to the public, and there is accountability, and all parties can be aware of the matter,” he said when winding up the debate on the Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026 for his ministry in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
Previously, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) reported that the e-Jamin system had been operating for five years since 2020 without a formal contract with the Federal Government.
The PAC said that of the RM193.71 million in bail deposits held in the account as of Dec 31, 2024, Dapat Vista was found to have invested RM130.8 million under the company’s name, generating annual interest of between RM4 million and RM5 million.
Elaborating, Kulasegaran said the PAC had previously put forward three options, namely for the government to purchase the e-Jamin system directly from Dapat Vista; subscribe to the system’s services and products; or pay the maintenance and operating costs before the system is eventually handed over to the government.
However, he said the Ministry of Finance, on Oct 22, 2025, rejected all three commercial proposals and decided to retain the existing system at no cost to the government through a formal agreement, along with a trustee bank structure.
He said the e-Jamin system enables court bail payments to be made online and completed within less than half an hour, compared with about five hours under the previous physical payment method.
Kulasegaran said the e-Jamin system was introduced in 2020 as a stop-gap measure, but its use continued to this day because of the convenience it provided to the public and legal practitioners.
He added that 81,667 bail cases had used the system up to last year, involving collections amounting to RM255.198 million, but audits revealed no instances of financial misappropriation.
Kulasegaran said the government had taken note of the issues related to the investment of bail funds by the company operating the system and acknowledged the need to clearly define the relationship and responsibilities between the government and the operator.
Meanwhile, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi, when winding up the debate on LKAN 2/2026 for his ministry, said a shortage of valuers at the Sabah Land and Survey Department (JTU) was among the main factors contributing to delays in the land acquisition process for the Phase 1 Sabah Pan Borneo Highway (LPB) project.
He said Sabah JTU currently has only seven valuers to handle valuation work statewide, affecting land acquisition and utility relocation at construction sites.
“In addition, the unsatisfactory performance of contractors is also among the causes of the delays. As such, Sabah Public Works Department officers have been instructed to conduct site inspections and ensure that contractors comply with the recovery plans,” he said.
To address the issue, he said the government was strengthening coordination with the state government through a steering committee co-chaired by the secretary-general of the Works Ministry and the Sabah State Secretary, as well as holding special state-level meetings to expedite the resolution of issues related to land acquisition and project implementation.
He said the Phase 1 Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project, comprising 35 work packages, had achieved physical progress of 89.01 per cent for Phase 1A, 37.5 per cent for WP09 and 23.96 per cent for Phase 1B.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting resumes at 10am today. — Bernama

Title: TNB’s additional tax claim won’t be passed to consumers via tariffs or affect dividends, says MOF
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The additional tax claim against Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) will not result in the cost being passed on to consumers through electricity tariff hikes, said the Ministry of Finance (MOF).
It said electricity tariffs in Peninsular Malaysia are determined by the Incentive-Based Regulation (IBR) framework and are subject to the government’s review and approval.
“TNB’s corporate tax liabilities are not costs that are automatically be passed on to consumers through electricity tariffs,” it said.
The ministry said this in a written reply to a question from Datuk Che Mohamad Zulkifly Jusoh (PN-Besut) regarding the implications of the additional tax claim on shareholder dividends and electricity tariffs.
According to the MOF, the claim also does not affect TNB’s ability to continue paying dividends, which is based on the company’s financial performance, cash position, and dividend policy.
“The government will continue to ensure that consumer interests are protected through existing tariff regulatory mechanisms, without compromising TNB’s ability to provide safe and reliable electricity supply,” it said. — Bernama

Title: MOF: Malaysia to pursue continued legal action, global cooperation for maximum 1MDB asset recovery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The government will continue to take legal action and strengthen international cooperation to maximise the recovery of the remaining misappropriated assets of 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB), according to the Ministry of Finance (MoF).
The ministry said that the effort is important to reduce the country’s financial burden and ensure the interests of the people are continuously protected.
As of August 31, 2026, the government had paid RM42.5 billion to cover commitments related to 1MDB, including principal payments, interest, legal fees and operational costs.
“If there is no additional fund recovery in the future, the government will still have to bear the remaining obligation of RM20.1 billion,” the MoF said.
The MoF stated this in a written response to Azli Yusof’s (PH-Shah Alam) question regarding the improvement measures following the Auditor General Report on public fund leakages, the current status of national asset recovery related to major financial scandals and the re-management of the recovered funds.
Regarding the status of asset recovery and the mechanism for the restructuring of funds related to the financial scandal, the ministry stated that the largest recovery activity at the moment involves 1MDB.
“The government has so far successfully recovered RM31.3 billion in asset recovery funds related to 1MDB,” it added. — Bernama

Title: Felda’s outstanding government-guaranteed loans stand at RM5.88b, says MOF
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The total outstanding government-guaranteed loans for the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) stood at RM5.88 billion as of September 30, 2026, after accounting for principal repayments totalling RM3.04 billion, according to the Ministry of Finance (MOF).
The ministry said the government had approved guarantees totaling RM9.9 billion for Felda to secure financing from local financial institutions and the capital market to fund projects, investments, and the Felda Recovery Plan.
“Of the total approved guarantees, Felda has obtained government-guaranteed financing amounting to RM8.92 billion, while RM980 million worth of government-guaranteed sukuk remains to be issued,” the ministry said.
The MOF said this in a written reply to a question from Azli Yusof (PH-Shah Alam) on the leakage of public funds and updates on efforts to recover state assets linked to financial scandals.
The ministry said the government had also agreed to provide an annual grant of RM990 million for 10 years to meet the annual principal repayments on the sukuk. — Bernama

Title: LCS 1 delivery pushed to April 2027, Defence Ministry issues damages notice to Lunas, says minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Lumut Naval Shipyard (Lunas), the company building Malaysia’s first Littoral Combat Ship (LCS 1), has set April 2027 as the new delivery date for the vessel to the Ministry of Defence (Mindef) under Phase 1.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Lunas had previously been unable to commit to or guarantee delivery by December this year.
“The delay will affect the readiness of the Malaysian Armed Forces and national defence.
“As the buyer, the ministry expects the LCS to be delivered. With the new date set for April 2027, we hope Lunas will have no further excuses or delays,” he said when winding up the debate on the Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) No. 2/2026 for the ministry in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
As such, Mindef has issued a notice of Liquidated Ascertained Damages (LAD) to Lunas as a demonstration of the government’s seriousness over the delay, he said.
Mohamed Khaled said Mindef, together with the Ministry of Finance, would take the necessary measures to monitor the project and ensure the new delivery date was met.
He said LCS 1 was 86.39 per cent complete as of August, but was still 13.61 percentage points behind schedule. The delay had been reduced by 0.27 percentage points.
Meanwhile, several issues raised in LKAN No. 2/2026 had also progressed, including the Integrated Logistics Support and Technical Aids contract, which was signed on Aug 26.
The contract enables various activities and tests on the vessel to proceed, as well as support work and training.
The procurement of 30mm Medium Calibre Gun ammunition and the Integrated Decoy Launching System is still under direct negotiation.
For the surface-to-air missile procurement, Mohamed Khaled said the Letter of Acceptance (SST) had been signed and the contract was expected to be finalised by mid-October.
He said Mindef was considering options from South Korea, Turkiye and France to ensure delivery and installation could be completed within a reasonable timeframe.
“We are weighing all these options and will ensure that delivery and installation do not take too long, unlike the Norway contract, which took up to eight years,” he said.
Mohamed Khaled also said the absence of the Naval Strike Missile did not mean the LCS would be delivered without weapons systems.
“The LCS will still be equipped with several other systems, including surface-to-air and surface-to-sea missiles to deal with various threats, including submarines.
“It will also have an electronic warfare system to counter attacks and a Combat Management System that integrates these capabilities with the vessel’s radar and detection systems,” he said
LKAN No. 2/2026, released on Monday, found that the LCS project was 7.55 per cent behind schedule as of June 25, with delays ranging from 30 to 108 days. — Bernama

Title: Minimum wage debate: What workers want, what employers say and what comes next
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia’s minimum wage is once again under the spotlight, with workers pushing for higher pay while employers warn against a steep increase as the federal government weighs its options ahead of Budget 2027.
The minimum wage is the statutory floor for basic pay that an employer must pay a covered worker — it does not include allowances, incentives or other additional payments.
But before getting into the arguments being made today, here is a quick look at how Malaysia’s minimum wage has changed over the years.
When did Malaysia introduce the minimum wage?
Malaysia’s minimum wage currently stands at RM1,700 a month.
But did you know it was not always at this level?
In fact, Malaysia first introduced a statutory minimum wage through the Minimum Wage Order (MWO) 2012, which took effect in January 2013, setting the country on a path of periodic wage increases.
The rate was initially set at RM900 a month in Peninsular Malaysia and RM800 in Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan.
The MWO was then amended in April 2016, raising the rate to RM1,000 a month in Peninsular Malaysia and RM920 in Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan, effective July that year.
It was amended again in 2018, when the government introduced a single nationwide rate of RM1,100 starting in January 2019, effectively removing the regional difference.
The MWO was amended for a third time in December 2019, when the government set the minimum wage at RM1,200 for urban areas and RM1,100 for rural areas, based on the locality of the relevant local authority, effective February 2020.
In April 2022, an amendment to the existing MWO was made and the government introduced a single nationwide minimum wage of RM1,500, which took effect in January 2023.
The most recent increase came in December 2024, when the government introduced the current minimum wage of RM1,700, which took effect in February 2025.
So where does the debate stand?
The next question, then, is when the minimum wage is due for review.
Under Section 25(1) of the National Wages Consultative Council Act, the Council is required to review the minimum wage order at least once every two years.
With the current RM1,700 rate having taken effect in 2025, the minimum wage is due for review by 2027.
Nevertheless, in August, the Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC) proposed raising the national minimum wage to RM3,100, describing it as a necessary “living wage” benchmark.
MTUC secretary-general Kamarul Baharin Mansor was quoted as saying the amount should be considered to reflect the rising costs of food, housing, transportation and other necessities.
He also called for expanding the wage structure to cover middle-income workers whose salaries have remained stagnant at the minimum rate, with some still earning RM1,700 despite a decade of service due to the lack of a defined salary progression framework.
In response, both the SME Association of Malaysia and Malaysia Retail Chain Association (MRCA) called on the government to defer any minimum wage increase for now, citing challenging operating conditions.
They cautioned that a blanket increase could severely strain SMEs already grappling with economic headwinds, saying they were not opposed to better wages but stressed that structural support was needed to help businesses absorb higher labour costs.
As for the government, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said in August that the National Wages Consultative Council would review the current minimum wage to decide whether to maintain or raise the rate.
However, by September, Ramanan said no decision had yet been made on a new minimum wage rate, adding that any announcement would only follow Cabinet approval.
With Budget 2027 set to be tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in the Dewan Rakyat on October 9, attention is now turning to whether the government will announce any changes to the current RM1,700 minimum wage.

Title: Haze: All Johor schools to close for two days starting tomorrow by  Regent’s decree over unhealthy API
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 7 — The Regent of Johor Tunku Mahkota Ismail has decreed for all schools in the state to close following the persistent haze and unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings,” said Johor Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali.
He explained that the two-day closure, starting tomorrow and the following day, was due to the ongoing haze compounded with a deteriorating air quality across all districts in the state.
“The closure affects 617,258 students across 1,198 schools that comes under the administration of the Education Ministry.
"All schools throughout Johor will be closed on October 8 and 9 as a precautionary measure to safeguard the student’s safety and health,” he said in a statement issued today.
Dr Muhammad Naqib pointed out that for schools involved in the Year 4 Learning Matrix (MPT4) or any other assessments, the implementation will be postponed and rescheduled.
He said this will be subjected to directives from the Johor Education Department (JPNJ) and relevant authorities.
“During the two-day closure period, Teaching and Learning at Home (PdPR) sessions will be conducted to ensure the learning process continues,” he said, adding that the state government and relevant agencies will continue to monitor API readings regularly.
Dr Muhammad Naqib said the state government understands that such a decision may impact parents and guardians who still need to work.
Therefore, he said the granting of appropriate work flexibility to affected parents or guardians by their employers will be greatly appreciated.
“I also urge parents to continue monitoring their children's health, ensure they stay hydrated and limit any outdoor activities.
“Parents or guardians need to seek immediate medical attention if their children experience coughing, sore throat or shortness of breath," he said.
Earlier, Johor recorded unhealthy API readings, with figures between 161 and 197, from eight monitoring stations.
Batu Pahat was the worst hit with an API reading of 197 in the morning.
Yesterday a total of 335 education institutions in the Batu Pahat district were ordered to close after the API reading in the district reached 208 last night.

Title: Laos meth bust: Four arrested in Subang Airport hangar raid over 521kg found in Learjet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) today raided a hangar at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang, believed to be linked to the seizure of 521 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs in Laos last week.
Port Klang AKPS Commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said the special operation was conducted jointly with the Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (JSJN), AKPS, Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters (IPD), Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad Auxiliary Police (AVSEC) and Special Branch Travel Control Officers (TCO).
“I can confirm that there was a raid and arrests. The operation was conducted jointly... we had been planning it since yesterday, and the operation began at noon today and has since been completed,” he told Bernama when contacted today.
Four individuals were reportedly arrested while preparing for a flight and were handed over to the Bukit Aman JSJN for further investigation.
However, Nik Ezanee declined to disclose details of the operation or the identities of the suspects, leaving it to the Bukit Aman JSJN to provide further information on the arrests.
On October 1, Laos police seized 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from a private Learjet that had arrived from Subang.
Following the seizure, 13 individuals, including a Malaysian, Singaporean and Filipino, were detained by the Laotian authorities to assist investigations into the cross-border drug trafficking case. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Budget 2027 to turn economic growth into better lives for Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Fifth Madani Budget is based on a clear resolve to strengthen the nation’s economy and translate growth into a better life for the people.
Anwar said he is aware that economic growth alone is insufficient if some citizens still face rising living costs.
Therefore, he said that Budget 2027 will continue to focus on alleviating burdens, protecting the people, creating opportunities, and ensuring that the benefits of development are felt more equitably.
“I will present all details this Friday, Insya-Allah,” he said in a post on X today.
Earlier today, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, briefed the media on the Madani 2027 Budget to explain the Madani government’s direction and efforts for the people.
The prime minister will present the Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat this Friday at 3.30pm. — Bernama

Title: Johor MB pushes for Asean emergency talks as haze hits unhealthy levels
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 7 — Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi called on the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) to play a more active role and to convene an emergency meeting to address the haze crisis.
He said the current transboundary haze situation is affecting Johor, particularly in the areas of public health and a deteriorating air quality in several areas of the state.
“Asean nations possessing the expertise, assets, and capabilities can step forward to assist based on needs, through coordination and mutual agreement.
“With effective cooperation, prevention, monitoring and response, efforts can be implemented immediately and effectively for the people across the region,” he said in a statement issued today.
Onn Hafiz hopes the proposal will be considered by Asean’s leadership to restore the situation and ensure the public can return to living in a safer and healthier environment.
He added that the proposal was raised during an earlier meeting with the Indonesian consul general in Johor Bahru Sigit Suryantoro Widiyanto.
“I conveyed the state government’s concerns and expressed hope that efforts to tackle the root causes of the haze can be further intensified.
“Our approach here is not to point fingers at any party, but rather to find a collective solution. The impact transcends our national borders,” he said.
Onn Hafiz explained that when air pollution crosses borders and affects neighboring countries, including Malaysia, the issue inevitably requires closer regional cooperation for mutual benefit.
Earlier today, Johor recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with figures between 161 and 197, in eight monitoring stations.
Batu Pahat was the worst hit with an API reading of 197 in the morning.
Yesterday a total of 335 education institutions in the Batu Pahat district were ordered to close today after the API reading in the district reached 208 last night.

Title: Former N. Sembilan exco members barred only from exco rooms but can still enter Wisma Negeri, says A-G
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The 10 state assemblymen who previously served as Negeri Sembilan executive councillors (exco) are only barred from entering their exco rooms following their dismissal from the posts on September 24, which means they are no longer members of the state administration.
However, they may still enter state government buildings in their capacity as elected representatives and carry out their duties as assemblymen, particularly to attend to matters involving their constituents.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said the ban also meant the former exco members were not allowed to enter their respective rooms, including to collect personal belongings left at the offices.
“As elected representatives, they can come to Wisma Negeri as usual to attend to official matters, but access to the exco rooms is not allowed because they are no longer members of the state administration,” he said when contacted today.
The media reported today that the 10 assemblymen — Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah — who are challenging the cancellation of their appointments as state exco members, have applied to the Seremban High Court to declare their dismissals null and void, invalid and of no effect.
All the plaintiffs filed originating summonses at the Seremban High Court through Messrs Hafarizam Wan & Aisha Mubarak last Monday against the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary and the Negeri Sembilan state government as defendants.
On whether any decisions had been made by the 10 former exco members before their dismissal, Mohd Dusuki said such decisions were valid and remained in force as they were still holding exco positions at the time.
“Decisions made while they were still exco members are valid. After their dismissal, they no longer have the authority to make decisions as exco members,” he said.

Title: Perak Perhilitan: Malayan tigers will only be captured if they threaten public safety
Article:
IPOH, Oct 7 — The Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) will only capture or translocate Malayan tigers if an assessment finds that their presence poses a threat to public safety.
Perak Perhilitan director Dr Pazil Abdul Patah said the assessment takes into account the tiger’s behaviour, frequency and duration of sightings, distance from residential areas, movement patterns, and evidence of interactions or attacks involving humans or livestock.
“If the assessment shows a clear and continuing threat to human safety, Perhilitan will take appropriate action based on technical assessments in the field,” he told Bernama.
Five tiger sightings or incidents have been recorded in Perak from January to October this year, beginning with a report of a roar in Proton City, Tanjung Malim on January 10, followed by an image captured in Bukit Bangkong, Chemor on July 14 and the capture of a tigress in Hulu Kinta on July 22.
This was followed by a fatal attack in Pos Perwor, Sungai Siput on September 21 and the discovery of tiger footprints at Kem Sultan Nazrin Shah, 69 Komando, Ulu Kinta on September 29.
Pazil said tiger sightings near human settlements did not necessarily mean that their forest habitat or roaming areas were shrinking, as movements could also be influenced by prey availability, habitat conditions, human disturbance, development and land use, as well as the animals’ natural movements.
“In some situations, tigers may move through forest edges or ecological corridors within their home range and be detected near human settlements by chance,” he said.
He said Perhilitan continuously monitored prey species such as barking deer, deer and wild boar in the state’s main forest reserves, with camera traps, field surveys and population data used to assess prey availability.
Pazil said complaints about tiger sightings were assessed based on the location, time, physical evidence and current situation to determine the priority and appropriate deployment of personnel, with control teams sent to the field when there was a risk to public safety.
He said besides physical measures such as setting traps, Perhilitan also provided technical advice and safety guidance, including advising residents in high-risk areas to avoid going out alone in the early morning or late evening, refrain from provoking tigers and leave the handling of such cases to the department. — Bernama

Title: Parliament’s Palestine Caucus to submit motion on Gaza genocide for debate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The Malaysian Parliament’s Palestine Caucus will submit a proposed motion on the genocide in Gaza to the Office of the Dewan Rakyat Speaker and seek to have it scheduled for debate during next week’s parliamentary sitting.
Its chairman Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said the proposed motion would include calls for a lasting ceasefire, the protection of civilians, and safe, sustained and unhindered access to humanitarian aid.
“Rejecting the forced displacement of Palestinians and affirming their right to self-determination, while supporting the processes of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and the International Criminal Court (ICC) within their respective jurisdictions, as well as respecting relevant international judicial decisions and orders,” he said.
Syed Ibrahim, who is also Deputy Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability, said this at a press conference held in conjunction with the Three-Year Commemoration of the Gaza Genocide at the Parliament building here today.
The Ledang Member of Parliament also said the motion would call for efforts to strengthen diplomatic action, including scrutiny of military assistance and arms transfers that risk facilitating violations of international law.
“In addition, to establish a coordinated Malaysian framework for the recovery of Gaza, prioritising healthcare, education, child rehabilitation and Palestinian-led reconstruction,” he said.
In this regard, Syed Ibrahim said the Caucus called for sufficient time to be allocated to allow for substantive debate and the participation of Members of Parliament from across the political divide.
“To ensure the success of this initiative, the Caucus calls for coordinated engagement with the government as well as government and opposition MPs to finalise the motion and facilitate its tabling and scheduling in accordance with the Standing Orders in force,” he said.
Meanwhile, he also called on the public to participate in the Three-Year Commemoration of the Gaza Genocide gathering from 2pm to 5pm this Friday, which will begin at Menara Tabung Haji before proceeding to the United States Embassy. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Education Ministry orders state and district education offices, schools to monitor haze, act based on API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has instructed state education departments (JPN), district education offices (PPD) and all educational institutions under its jurisdiction to continue monitoring the current haze situation in their respective locations to determine further action.
It said the directive includes immediately suspending all outdoor activities, including outdoor gatherings and sports, particularly in areas with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings exceeding 100.
“The ministry is always monitoring the situation and prioritises the welfare, health and safety of students, especially when facing unexpected haze conditions.
“The haze situation has also resulted in several locations posting unhealthy API readings,” it said in a statement today.
It said educational institutions in the Batu Pahat district, under the supervision of the Johor JPN, are temporarily closed starting today until conditions are safe and further instructions are issued.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Batu Pahat recorded an API reading of 190 as of 10 am today.
Following the closure, home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) will be implemented based on suitability and current directives, taking into account the students’ safety, health and well-being.
“Based on the current haze situation and the latest API readings recorded nationwide, the Johor JPN has taken follow-up measures in accordance with the guidelines established by the MOE,” it added.
MOE also advised the JPN, PPD and all educational institutions under its purview to implement preventive measures outlined in the guidelines, including postponing all outdoor activities during periods of extreme heat or haze and immediately closing any school located in an area or district where the API reading exceeds 200.
It also urged schools to remain vigilant and coordinate with nearby clinics or hospitals should any students experience health complications due to the haze and hot weather.
“The JPN, PPD and all educational institutions under the MOE must also remain vigilant and monitor API readings and the latest status via the DOE’s website at https://eqms.doe.gov.my/APIMS/main on a regular basis to safeguard the health of students and the education community,” it added.
Yesterday, the Batu Pahat District Disaster Management Committee issued a directive for all schools, kindergartens and childcare centres in the district to close from today after the API reading there reached 203 as of 8pm.
The closure involved all 176 MOE-run schools in Batu Pahat, comprising 144 primary schools, 31 secondary schools and one vocational college.
Following this, state Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said in a statement that 106 state government religious schools, including  Integrated Religious Primary Schools (SRAB), and 53 registered private Islamic educational institutions (IPIS) in Batu Pahat have also been ordered to close, effective today. — Bernama

Title: Witness insists Publika office existed in Hamzah Zainudin aide’s RM350,000 corruption trial
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — A witness in the corruption trial involving a former political secretary to former home minister Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today maintained that the office of Yayasan Tanah Aku in Publika, the alleged location for the handover of RM350,000 in commission to Sayed Amir Muzzakkir Al Sayed Mohamad, did exist.
Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof, 51, managing director of Nexuscorpgroup Sdn Bhd (NSB), said this during cross-examination by counsel Datuk Yaacob Md Sam, appearing for Sayed Amir Muzzakkir.
Yaacob:
I put it to you that the handover of RM100,000 on December 4, 2020 and RM250,000 on December 16, 2020 to Sayed Amir Muzzakkir did not take place, because the said office did not exist.
Wan Azhar:
I disagree.
In his witness statement, Wan Azhar stated that Sayed Amir Muzzakkir asked him to pay RM350,000 in cash as part of a five per cent commission, after assisting NSB secure a Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) project tender.
“I handed over RM100,000 in a paper bag to Sayed around 4pm on December 4, 2020, and RM250,000, also in a paper bag, at 3.30pm on December 16, 2020. On both occasions, only Sayed and I were present,” he said in his witness statement.
The 17th prosecution witness said he had accompanied a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer to Publika to identify the said location, and found the unit in question to be closed, with no signage indicating that it was the office of Yayasan Tanah Aku.
Wan Azhar, however, disagreed with Yaacob’s suggestion that both units were vacant and unoccupied on the said dates.
Yaacob:
The owner of the premises gave evidence that, prior to the signing of the tenancy agreement, both units had been occupied by a law firm. That firm vacated the premises at the end of 2019. We therefore put it to you that from the end of 2019 until January 1, 2021, no office occupied either unit. Do you agree?
Wan Azhar:
I went to the location only twice, on December 4 and 16, 2020. I therefore know only that it was in operation on those two dates. On other days, I cannot be certain whether it was in operation or vacant.
On May 23, 2024, Sayed Amir Muzzakkir, 44, was charged on two counts of receiving RM350,000 in gratification from Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof as inducement for assisting NSB secure the RMPNet tender for PDRM valued at RM381,112,042.44.
The offences allegedly occurred at the office of Yayasan Tanah Aku, Solaris Dutamas, here, at 4pm on December 4, 2020 and at 3.30pm on December 16, 2020, respectively.
Sayed Amir Muzzakkir was also charged with soliciting RM350,000 in gratification from the same individual, for a similar purpose, at the Shah Alam office of NSB in early December 2020.
The charges were brought under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years’ imprisonment and a fine of not less than five times the value of the gratification or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
The trial before Judge Rosli Ahmad resumes tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Selangor Sultan receives Silver Jubilee Keris marking 25 years on throne
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 7 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah today received the presentation of the Keris Jubli Perak, specially crafted to commemorate His Royal Highness’s 25th year on the Selangor throne.
According to a post on the Selangor Royal Office Facebook page, the ceremonial
keris
was specially commissioned as an expression of Sultan Sharafuddin’s deep appreciation for the art, heritage and diverse traditions associated with the Malay
keris
.
The
keris
was meticulously crafted to reflect the significance and uniqueness of the Sultan of Selangor’s Silver Jubilee celebrations.
Among the skilled artisans and craftsmen involved in the making of this historic
keris
were Datuk Dr Abdul Muati Zamri Ahmad, Datuk Wan Burhanuddin Wan Hassan and Datuk Mohamed Raffe Chekku, with the project led by Rafulin Foundation.
“The entire production process took 12 months, with each component crafted meticulously and in detail,” according to the post.
The Keris Jubli Perak is a symbolic work that chronicles Sultan Sharafuddin’s reign through the art of Malay heritage.
“Every material, measurement and decorative element carries its own meaning, reflecting the journey of the Sultan’s reign and the identity of Selangor.
“The
keris
measures 25 inches in length to commemorate 25 years of His Royal Highness’ reign, while the use of seven types of iron symbolises the unity of strength. The White Eagle element represents courage and authority,” the post said.
The
keris
also incorporates Black Healer wood as a symbol linking Malay heritage with traditional beliefs, while buffalo horn represents resilience and the refinement of craftsmanship.
In addition, nine gemstones are inlaid into the
keris
to represent the nine districts of Selangor.
“Twenty-five chevron-shaped motifs symbolise and commemorate the journey of His Royal Highness’ reign, spanning the past and present while carrying hopes for the future,” according to the post.
The making of the
keris
also reflects the richness of Malay heritage and the dedication of the artisans in preserving and elevating the traditional art of keris craftsmanship for future generations. — Bernama

Title: Perak MB tells accuser to prove allegations over special officer’s mosque speech
Article:
IPOH, Oct 7 — Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad today said that he was unsure of the veracity of an allegation that his special officer had delivered an official speech at a mosque in Kerian, stressing that the accuser must prove the claim.
Saarani said the Sultan of Perak’s decree must be obeyed and that even he, despite being the chairman of state religious affairs, would not dare to deliver a speech at any mosque.
“I am not sure about the authenticity of the activity. But if it happened, he cannot do so. To me, it is very simple — His Royal Highness’s decree must be obeyed.
“However the person making the allegation must prove it. We cannot simply make such a reckless accusation,” he told reporters after attending the closing ceremony of Perak Innovation Convention at the Stadium Indera Mulia here.
Saarani was responding to allegations that had gone viral claiming that his special officer had delivered an official speech at a programme held at a mosque in Kerian, which was alleged to have contravened the Sultan of Perak’s decree.
The allegations were made by Perak PAS Youth Strategy Director Nurhafizul Badrul Hisham via his Facebook posting, who raised questions about compliance with the Perak Sultan’s decree barring politicians from delivering speeches at mosques and surau.
Nurhafizul said the matter should be taken seriously as the ban had also been enforced through an official circular issued by the Perak Islamic Religious Department (JAIPk).
Asked about calls for an investigation and for the officer to be suspended if the allegation was proven true, Saarani said the matter also involved the chairman of the mosque committee.
“It is like this. It also involves the chairman of the mosque committee itself. Any activity that is to be held must be known to and approved by the chairman of the mosque committee.
“There have been several cases before, including one in Kuala Kangsar recently, where the matter was brought to the Islamic Religious Council for investigation, and the chairman of the mosque committee concerned was called in,” he said.
“So, if it is true the incident did happened, then we will ask the special officer concerned to apologise,” he added.

Title: Malaysia pushes to fast-track Indonesia talks on forest fire aid as haze worsens
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — Malaysia wants operational negotiations with Indonesia to be expedited to allow the country’s team to be sent to help extinguish the forest fires in that country, which have caused cross-border haze.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said that the agreement with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto regarding Malaysia’s offer of assistance has been obtained, but operational methods and the location of the Malaysian team are still under negotiation between the two countries.
“However, the way the operation will be carried out is probably being negotiated between both parties, both countries.
“I hope that the negotiations for this operation, on how and where the team from Malaysia that can help can be expedited because the haze situation in our country has become extremely severe, exceeding unhealthy levels, and is approaching the hazardous index,” he said to the media.
He said this when met after attending the graduation ceremony of the Diploma in Diplomacy Programme 2026 here today.
Mohamad said he hopes that matters related to the operation can be decided quickly so that Malaysia can send a team to help their friends in Indonesia extinguish the extensive and spreading forest fires, especially in Kalimantan.
“I personally hope that the operational issues between the two can be expedited and decided so that we can send a team to assist,” he said.
Previously, the media reported that Indonesia accepted Malaysia’s offer to help extinguish the forest fires in the republic that caused prolonged haze for several weeks.
The matter was announced by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi during his working visit to Indonesia last month.
Ahmad Zahid was reported to have said that Prabowo agreed to Malaysia’s offer to help extinguish forest fires in Kalimantan, with more than 1,400 hotspots detected. — Bernama

Title: Nhaveen murder trial adjourned to tomorrow after defence seeks time over witness statements
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 7 — The High Court here today adjourned the defence proceedings of four men charged with the murder of teenager T. Nhaveen to tomorrow.
The defence sought an adjournment on the ground that it required time to follow up on the delivery of four witness statements to the prosecution today.
Judge Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid allowed the application and fixed the proceedings to resume at 9.30am tomorrow.
Counsel Maanveer Singh Dhillon, appearing for the four accused, informed the court that the defence had limited time to meet them in prison to prepare the said witness statements.
“We have just finalised the (written) witness statement. It is ready. We will deliver it to the prosecution today,” he said.
In addition, he submitted that the prosecution likewise required time to scrutinise the statements delivered today before the defence proceedings could continue.
Deputy public prosecutors Mohd Amri Johari and Yazid Mustaqim Roslan appeared for the prosecution, while the four accused were represented by counsel Maanveer Singh, R. Thevan and Lim Sheng Zhe.
On July 3, the High Court fixed October 7 to 9 and 12 to 16 for the defence trial of the four men charged with the murder of Nhaveen, nine years ago.
Previously, the Court of Appeal ordered J. Ragesuthan, 27, S. Gokulan, 27, and two other individuals who were juveniles at the time of the incident to enter their defence on the charge of murdering Nhaveen.
That decision was made after the court allowed the prosecution’s appeal against the High Court’s decision acquitting and discharging them on October 3, 2023.
They were charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code with murder, and under Section 326 of the same law with voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons, in respect of Nhaveen, 18, at the same place, date and time.
The panel of judges also directed that the case be remitted to the Penang High Court for the defence stage.
The four accused were likewise ordered to enter their defence on the charge of causing injury to Nhaveen’s friend, T. Previin, near the Karpal Singh Learning Centre on Jalan Kaki Bukit, Gelugor, between 11pm and midnight on June 9, 2017.
Nhaveen died on June 15, 2017, from severe injuries sustained in the incident, after six days of treatment at Penang Hospital. — Bernama

Title: Sun bear still on the loose as Perhilitan widens Seremban search
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 7 — Police have stepped up patrols around Taman Tuanku Ja’afar (TTJ) after a sun bear was spotted in the residential area, with authorities widening the search as the animal remains uncaught.
Seremban district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Yatim Osman said the patrols were aimed at helping keep residents safe amid concerns that the bear could approach or attack people,
Harian Metro
reported today.
“Although this falls under the jurisdiction of the Department of Wildlife and National Parks we are also helping by patrolling the surrounding areas to detect the animal,” he said.
“At least the presence of police personnel on patrols will discourage the animal from approaching residential areas and make residents feel safer, but I advise them to remain vigilant,” he said.
The department, commonly known as Perhilitan (the Malay abbreviation of Jabatan Perlindungan Hidupan Liar dan Taman Negara), is conducting the search with the help of its personnel and members of the public, while police are assisting with efforts to safeguard residents.
Negeri Sembilan Perhilitan director Wan Mat Wan Harun said the department had widened its search after the bear failed to enter a trap set nearby.
“Perhilitan is still monitoring and tracking the bear’s movements around TTJ and nearby areas.
“For now, we are carrying out monitoring within a wider search area,” he was quoted as saying.
Wan Mat said this was the first report the department had received of a sun bear entering the TTJ residential area.
He said Perhilitan had previously received information about a sun bear at Kem 15 Rejimen Askar Melayu Diraja in Senawang, next to Taman Tuanku Ja’afar, on September 19.
“The animal was believed to have entered the residential area because it was hungry and looking for food, and the bee nests kept at the camp were raided by the bear,” he said.
The search follows a video uploaded to TikTok showing the animal tearing into the roof of a hut in the housing area at about midnight last Sunday.
The sun bear is the world’s smallest bear species and is native to South-east Asia, including Malaysia.
It is classified as vulnerable on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List, with its population declining due mainly to habitat loss, hunting and human-bear conflict.
As a forest-dependent animal, sun bears can occasionally venture into human settlements in search of food, bringing them into potentially dangerous encounters with residents.

Title: Two senior students to face murder charge tomorrow over Kuala Pilah sports school death
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 7 — Two 16-year-old boys suspected of involvement in the death of a younger boy at a sports school in Kuala Pilah last month are expected to be charged with murder tomorrow, Berita Harian reported.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said that the investigation papers had been referred to the state prosecution office.
“Both suspects will be brought to the Kuala Pilah Magistrate’s Court at 9.30am tomorrow,” he was quoted as saying.
He said the prosecution had instructed that both suspects be charged with murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, which deals with acts done by several people with a common intention.
According to media reports at the time, the 14-year-old was found unconscious at the school hostel at about 8pm on September 25.
He was taken to Hospital Tuanku Ampuan Najihah in Kuala Pilah, where he was pronounced dead.
His body was then sent to the forensic medicine department at Hospital Tuanku Ja’afar in Seremban for a post-mortem.
Police subsequently detained two 16-year-old boys, who are seniors of the victim, to assist investigations and classified the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Alzafny previously said the remand of the first suspect is extended until tomorrow, while the second suspect’s remand is extended until October 9.

Title: Higher Education Ministry says institutions given autonomy to adjust learning mode when API exceeds 201
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — Higher education institutions (IPTs) in areas recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings above 201 have been given the flexibility to determine suitable teaching and learning (PdP) modes to reduce health risks while ensuring students’ education continues
In a statement today, the Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) said it was closely monitoring air quality and had directed all institutions under its purview to monitor API readings in their respective areas.
Outdoor activities should also be assessed and adjusted according to the latest readings.
The ministry advised IPT communities to refer to official information from the Department of Environment (DOE) and follow the guidelines issued by their respective institutions.
“MOHE will continue to monitor the situation and adjust the operations of IPTs to safeguard the health, well-being and welfare of all its members,” it said.
Bernama reported that 35 areas recorded unhealthy API readings as of 10 am today.
According to the DOE’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Batu Pahat, Johor, and Johan Setia, Selangor recorded the highest readings at 190 each, followed by Cheras, Kuala Lumpur, and Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, at 189 each, and Putrajaya at 187.
API readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous. — Bernama
